I want to write about attention. Not the kind you pay in school, but the kind you give when you're standing at a window at dusk, watching the sky go from blue to gray to something almost purple, and you're not waiting for anything. You're just there. That kind of attention feels rare now. Everything asks for something—your click, your like, your opinion, your outrage. But the sky doesn't ask. It just changes, and if you're lucky, you notice.

I've been thinking about how much of life is made of things that don't ask for anything. The smell of rain on hot pavement. The way a dog tilts its head when it hears a word it almost knows. The sound of a page turning in a quiet room. These moments don't demand to be remembered. They just pass. And yet, when I try to recall what actually mattered in a day, it's rarely the big things. It's the small, unasked-for ones.

Maybe that's what freedom is. Not the absence of constraints, but the presence of attention. Being able to stop, even for a second, and let the world be what it is without trying to use it. To look at a tree and not think about its name or its age or whether it needs pruning. Just to look.

I don't know if I'm good at that. Most of the time I'm narrating, planning, worrying, comparing. My mind is a committee meeting that never ends. But sometimes, in the middle of washing dishes or walking to the mailbox, there's a gap. A pause. And in that pause, everything feels okay. Not because anything changed, but because for a moment I wasn't trying to change anything.

That's what I wanted to write about, I guess. The gaps. The pauses. The moments that don't ask for anything, and the strange, quiet joy of giving them your attention anyway.
